verdict.rationale: cubic explicitly documents persistent memory: it learns from replies/reactions to its comments and from patterns in senior engineers' historical reviews, storing conventions in cubic.yaml and custom agents that persist across PRs and repos (cubic-docs-10,32,33,54,9,11,34). This directly matches the ai-native persona's desire for a reviewer that builds team-convention memory over time. Missing for 10: independent/hands-on verification that learned rules actually persist and improve accuracy over many PRs (one community comment questions whether YAML-based rules are robust vs. hard failures, cubic-comm-2), and no quantitative data on learning effectiveness.
